L0@P0: DIRECTIVE 2026-48
L1@P0: October 2, 2026
L2@P0: To: All County Boards of Elections
L3@P0: Board Members, Directors, and Deputy Directors
L4@P0: Re: Canvass and Certification of the November 3, 2026, General Election
L5@P0: SUMMARY
L6@P0: This directive outlines the procedures that boards of elections must follow when
L7@P0: conducting both the Unofficial and the Official Canvasses of the November 3, 2026,
L8@P0: General Election.
L9@P0: To assist boards of elections with any problems, questions, or concerns on Election Day,
L10@P0: the Secretary of State’s office is staffed on Election Day from 6 a.m. until all boards
L11@P0: report their unofficial results to our office. Boards should contact the Secretary of State’s
L12@P0: office using a dedicated phone number that will be emailed before November 3, 2026.
L13@P0: All directors, deputy directors, and board members must ensure that they are able to
L14@P0: receive emails and other communications sent from the Secretary of State’s office via a
L15@P0: .gov email address on November 3, 2026 (including after the polls close).
L16@P0: PART ONE - UNOFFICIAL CANVASS
L17@P0: The Unofficial Canvass of the November 3, 2026, General Election must be conducted on
L18@P0: election night in accordance with state law1 and the processes and procedures outlined
L19@P0: in Chapter 10, Section 10.03 of the Election Official Manual (EOM). Each board of
L20@P0: elections must ensure all eligible Election Day and absentee ballots are tabulated and
L21@P0: reported in its Unofficial Canvass. Boards must ensure all memory cards containing
L22@P0: tabulated results are properly processed within their election management system
L23@P0: (EMS). Each board must have a dedicated document to ensure it meets this requirement
L24@P0: (e.g., a checklist or chart to check off once a memory card is processed).
L25@P0: 1 See R.C. 3505.27 (requiring the counting of regular ballots that were cast at precinct polling locations); R.C.
L26@P0: 3509.06 (requiring the counting of eligible absentee ballots); R.C. 3511.11(A)-(B) (requiring the counting of
L27@P0-1: uniformed service and overseas voter absentee ballots).Office of the Ohio Secretary of State 2 | page
L28@P1: Boards must also maintain strict inventory control over all USB drives used during
L29@P1: testing and mock election activities. USB drives containing mock election or test data
L30@P1: must be clearly identified, accounted for, and stored for retention before Election Day.
L31@P1: Boards must have a documented process to verify that only USB drives properly
L32@P1: prepared for the current election are used. This process must prevent any USB drive
L33@P1: containing mock election or test data from being introduced into the EMS during
L34@P1: Election Night Reporting.
L35@P1: The Unofficial Canvass must be conducted in full view of the members of the board of
L36@P1: elections and any appointed observers, and the board must continuously count the
L37@P1: ballots throughout the Unofficial Canvass.2
L38@P1: I. PROCESSING ABSENTEE BALLOTS
L39@P1: Boards of elections may begin processing (including scanning, but not tabulating)
L40@P1: absentee ballots on October 6, 2026, the day after the close of voter registration. Boards
L41@P1: must begin this process prior to Election Day to ensure the Unofficial Canvass includes
L42@P1: all absentee ballots received by the close of polls on November 3, 2026. Ohio law
L43@P1: prohibits boards from tabulating any absentee ballot prior to 7:31 p.m. on Election Day.3
L44@P1: If a court orders polls to remain open later than 7:30 p.m. on Election Day, boards will
L45@P1: receive a directive with specific instructions.
L46@P1: II. ELECTION NIGHT REPORTING (ENR)
L47@P1: State law requires boards of elections to provide election results for certain contests to
L48@P1: the Secretary of State’s office.4 Election Night Reporting (ENR) for the November 3,
L49@P1: 2026, General Election will consist of results for the following races:
L50@P1: • Governor and Lieutenant Governor
L51@P1: • Attorney General
L52@P1: • Auditor of State
L53@P1: • Secretary of State
L54@P1: • Treasurer of State
L55@P1: • Justice of the Supreme Court (Full term commencing 1/1/2027)
L56@P1: • Justice of the Supreme Court (Full term commencing 1/2/2027)
L57@P1: • U.S. Senator (Unexpired term ending 1/3/2029)
L58@P1-2: 2 R.C. 3505.27; R.C. 3505.29; R.C. 3505.30. 3 R.C. 3509.06(F). 4 R.C. 3505.27(C).Office of the Ohio Secretary of State 3 | page
L59@P2: • Representative to Congress
L60@P2: • State Senator
L61@P2: • State Representative
L62@P2: • Judge of the Court of Appeals
L63@P2: • Judge of the Court of Common Pleas
L64@P2: • County Court Judge
L65@P2: • County Commissioner
L66@P2: • County Auditor
L67@P2: • County Office (if a vacancy occurred that requires an unexpired term election)
L68@P2: • Statewide Issue 3
L69@P2: All counties must use the Secretary of State’s County Submission System (CSS) to
L70@P2: provide summary results for Statewide Issue 3 and all candidates that appear on the
L71@P2: county’s ballot.
L72@P2: Although boards of elections will have access to manually key the results within the time
L73@P2: frames below, the upload tool allows each board to do so more efficiently and
L74@P2: accurately by mitigating data entry errors. Boards must use the secure USB drives
L75@P2: provided by the Secretary of State’s office to ensure the security of the ENR system and
L76@P2: EMS. The USB drives must be used only once.
L77@P2: For the Unofficial Canvass, boards must provide summary-level election results, rather
L78@P2: than precinct-level results. Boards will upload precinct-level results for the Official
L79@P2: Canvass.
L80@P2: A. Initial Reporting
L81@P2: Each board of elections must log in to the CSS no later than 7:45 p.m. on November 3,
L82@P2: 2026. A board must immediately notify Secretary of State personnel if they experience
L83@P2: any delays in completing any portion of the results reporting activity.
L84@P2: Each board of elections must upload vote totals for absentee ballots by 8 p.m., unless
L85@P2: the voting system is technologically unable to do so. If necessary, counties may upload
L86@P2: partial absentee results. If a board uploads partial absentee results at 8 p.m., it must not
L87@P2: double-report the initial upload. Contact the board’s voting system vendor if you need
L88@P2: technical assistance. The board must enter zero precincts reporting when it uploads its
L89@P2-3: absentee results. Office of the Ohio Secretary of State 4 | page
L90@P3: B. Reporting Schedule
L91@P3: ENR begins with the first upload of absentee results by 8 p.m. and will continue at
L92@P3: the assigned time throughout the night. After the board uploads its first summary
L93@P3: election results, it must report on one of the following time increments assigned to the
L94@P3: county:
L95@P3: 1. “Half-Hour” Counties
L96@P3: Allen, Ashtabula, Athens, Belmont, Butler, Clark, Clermont, Columbiana, Cuyahoga,
L97@P3: Delaware, Erie, Fairfield, Franklin, Geauga, Greene, Hamilton, Hancock, Jefferson, Knox,
L98@P3: Lake, Lawrence, Licking, Lorain, Lucas, Mahoning, Marion, Medina, Miami, Montgomery,
L99@P3: Muskingum, Portage, Richland, Ross, Sandusky, Scioto, Stark, Summit, Trumbull,
L100@P3: Tuscarawas, Union, Warren, Washington, Wayne, and Wood counties.
L101@P3: “Half-hour” counties must report at each half hour beginning at 8:15 p.m. and every
L102@P3: half hour thereafter (e.g., 8:45 p.m., 9:15 p.m., 9:45 p.m., etc.) and must continue
L103@P3: reporting until all precincts report results.
L104@P3: A board of elections must notify Secretary of State personnel if there will be a delay in
L105@P3: reporting results. After 100 percent of the precincts have reported, boards must enter
L106@P3: the final vote tallies into their CSS. The board does not have to wait until its designated
L107@P3: reporting time before reporting the final results.
L108@P3: 2. “Hourly” Counties
L109@P3: “Top-of-the-hour” counties (e.g., 8 p.m., 9 p.m., etc.): Ashland, Auglaize, Brown,
L110@P3: Champaign, Clinton, Crawford, Darke, Defiance, Fulton, Guernsey, Highland, Huron,
L111@P3: Logan, Madison, Mercer, Morrow, Ottawa, Pickaway, Preble, Seneca, Shelby, and
L112@P3: Williams counties.
L113@P3: “Bottom-of-the-hour” counties (e.g., 8:30 p.m., 9:30 p.m., etc.): Adams, Carroll,
L114@P3: Coshocton, Fayette, Gallia, Hardin, Harrison, Henry, Hocking, Holmes, Jackson, Meigs,
L115@P3: Monroe, Morgan, Noble, Paulding, Perry, Pike, Putnam, Van Wert, Vinton, and Wyandot
L116@P3: counties.
L117@P3: Note: “Bottom-of-the-hour” counties will report once at the “Top-of-the-hour” at 8 p.m.
L118@P3: and then at the bottom hour as noted above.
L119@P3: “Hourly” counties must report summary election results at the top or bottom of every
L120@P3: hour, as specified above, and continue reporting until all precincts have reported. If the
L121@P3-4: board reports more frequently than that, it must still report on the hour. Office of the Ohio Secretary of State 5 | page
L122@P4: A board must notify Secretary of State personnel if it will be delayed in reporting results.
L123@P4: After 100 percent of the precincts have reported, boards must enter the final vote tallies
L124@P4: into their CSS. The board does not have to wait until its designated reporting time
L125@P4: before reporting the final results.
L126@P4: C. Supplemental Statistics
L127@P4: Boards of elections must provide supplemental statistics upon reporting the county’s
L128@P4: last precinct or shortly thereafter. Boards must promptly report vote totals, even if
L129@P4: supplemental statistics are not yet available. On election night, upload the election
L130@P4: results first and then submit the statistics when available. The required supplemental
L131@P4: statistics are as follows:
L132@P4: Counted Ballots
L133@P4: • Total regular Election Day ballots cast and counted from Election Day
L134@P4: precincts (do not include absentee).
L135@P4: • Total absentee ballots, including early in person and by mail, counted.
L136@P4: • Total regular Election Day and absentee ballots cast and counted as part of
L137@P4: the Unofficial Canvass.
L138@P4: Outstanding Ballots
L139@P4: • Total number of outstanding UOCAVA absentee ballots (issued but not yet
L140@P4: counted).
L141@P4: • Total number of provisional ballots (issued at the polls or the board office
L142@P4: before or on Election Day).
L143@P4: III. SUMMARY AND FINAL REPORTS
L144@P4: Boards of elections must follow the procedures outlined in Chapter 10, Section 10.03 of
L145@P4: the Election Official Manual for reporting summary results and submitting final summary
L146@P4: reports in even-numbered year elections. The required reports and forms (listed below)
L147@P4: for the Unofficial Canvass as well as the instructions and deadline for submission will be
L148@P4: provided to boards of elections via email before Election Day:
L149@P4: • Unofficial Vote Total Summary Report
L150@P4: • Group Detail Report (if not included with Summary Report)
L151@P4: • Write-In Report
L152@P4: • Most Populous Report(s) (when applicable)
L153@P4-5: • Signature Form Office of the Ohio Secretary of State 6 | page
L154@P5: In addition to the Unofficial Vote Total Summary Report submitted on election night,
L155@P5: each board must print their county results from their CSS via the “Current County
L156@P5: Results” page and proof this report against the results from their EMS. The Unofficial
L157@P5: Vote Total Summary Report, Group Detail Report, and the Signature Form must be
L158@P5: emailed to Results@OhioSoS.gov. Instructions outlining this requirement will be
L159@P5: provided separately.
L160@P5: On election night, after the Secretary of State’s office receives, reviews, and compares
L161@P5: the board’s Unofficial Vote Total Summary Report and Group Detail Report, a Secretary
L162@P5: of State staff member will contact the director.
L163@P5: The director and deputy director must not leave the office until Secretary of State staff
L164@P5: contacts the director to confirm that the board’s reports have been received and
L165@P5: reviewed to ensure the results match. The director is responsible for releasing the
L166@P5: board’s staff.
L167@P5: PART TWO - POST-ELECTION CURE PERIOD
L168@P5: I. DAYS AND HOURS
L169@P5: Each board of elections conducting an election must be open to the public on each of
L170@P5: the four calendar days immediately following Election Day and during the hours
L171@P5: specified below to allow voters to cure a deficiency on an absentee or provisional ballot,
L172@P5: as provided for in state law:5
L173@P5: • Wednesday, November 4, 2026 8 a.m. – 5 p.m.
L174@P5: • Thursday, November 5, 2026 8 a.m. – 5 p.m.
L175@P5: • Friday, November 6, 2026 8 a.m. – 5 p.m.
L176@P5: • Saturday, November 7, 2026 8 a.m. – 5 p.m.
L177@P5: If a board of elections has no voters with a deficiency on their absentee or provisional
L178@P5: ballot after Election Day (i.e., there is nothing possible to cure for any voter that cast a
L179@P5: ballot in the election) or all deficiencies have been cured, the board may return to its
L180@P5: normal operating hours for the remainder of the cure period.
L181@P5-6: 5 R.C. 3503.201(D)(2); R.C. 3505.181(B)(7)-(8); R.C. 3509.06(D)(3)(b).Office of the Ohio Secretary of State 7 | page
L182@P6: II. AFFIDAVITS OF RELIGIOUS OBJECTION6
L183@P6: A provisional voter who failed to provide a valid photo ID has four days after Election
L184@P6: Day to either appear at the board of elections office to show a valid photo ID or
L185@P6: complete an Affidavit of Religious Objection (Form-12-O).
L186@P6: To cure a provisional ballot for lack of valid photo ID, it is not sufficient to provide a
L187@P6: copy of the photo ID, the Ohio driver license number, or the state ID card number, or
L188@P6: the last four digits of the voter’s Social Security number (SSN). The voter must show a
L189@P6: valid photo ID (not a copy) by the fourth day after Election Day.
L190@P6: If the voter did not have a photo ID because of a religious objection to being
L191@P6: photographed and the voter did not complete Form 12-O at the time they voted a
L192@P6: provisional ballot, the voter must appear at the board office and complete the affidavit
L193@P6: by the fourth day after Election Day (Saturday, November 7, 2026).
L194@P6: No later than 6 p.m. on Saturday, November 7, 2026, boards of elections must transmit
L195@P6: the information in the completed affidavits to the Secretary of State’s office, which then
L196@P6: must consult the Bureau of Motor Vehicles’ (BMV) database to determine whether the
L197@P6: BMV issued a currently unexpired photo ID to that voter. The Secretary of State’s office
L198@P6: will complete this verification no later than the seventh day after Election Day. The
L199@P6: Affidavit of Religious Objection is not valid if the BMV has issued a currently unexpired
L200@P6: photo ID or if the last four digits of the voter’s SSN provided on the affidavit do not
L201@P6: match those digits in the Statewide Voter Registration Database (SWVRD). To compile
L202@P6: the information for each voter, each board must supply the necessary data either by
L203@P6: export from the voter registration system or by completion of a spreadsheet that will be
L204@P6: provided with instructions under separate cover.
L205@P6: III. EXAMINING AND COUNTING PROVISIONAL BALLOTS
L206@P6: Boards of elections must follow the “Mandatory Step-by-Step Process for Determining
L207@P6: Eligibility” procedures outlined in Chapter 8, Section 8.05 of the Election Official Manual.
L208@P6: Board staff, working in bipartisan teams, may begin examining provisional ballot
L209@P6: envelopes the day after the election, as long as the board has adopted a provisional
L210@P6: ballot policy allowing its staff to do so. The bipartisan teams may categorize provisional
L211@P6: ballots into groups of like ballots (e.g., ballots that have been verified and eligible to be
L212@P6-7: 6 R.C. 3505.181(B)(7); R.C. 3505.182(D)(1)-(3); R.C. 3505.183(B)(3)(d); R.C. 3505.19(C).Office of the Ohio Secretary of State 8 | page
L213@P7: counted, provisional affirmations that are missing the voter’s signature, etc.) for the
L214@P7: board to consider. However, the board must not examine the provisional ballot
L215@P7: affirmation of any provisional ballot cast by an individual who must provide photo ID,
L216@P7: complete an affidavit of religious objection, or provide additional information to
L217@P7: determine the individual’s eligibility until the individual does so or until the fifth day
L218@P7: after Election Day, whichever is earlier.7
L219@P7: It is important to remember that only the board members themselves can determine the
L220@P7: validity of each provisional ballot. The board must, by a majority vote, determine
L221@P7: whether to accept and count the provisional ballots in a properly noticed public
L222@P7: meeting. No provisional ballot envelope may be opened or counted until the board has
L223@P7: voted on the eligibility of every provisional ballot cast in the election.8
L224@P7: IV. CURING ABSENTEE BALLOT DEFECTS
L225@P7: Whenever a board of elections receives an absentee ballot identification envelope that is
L226@P7: missing required information or that contains information that does not conform to the
L227@P7: voter’s registration record, the board of elections must contact the absentee voter to
L228@P7: provide an opportunity to supplement their identification envelope so the voter’s ballot
L229@P7: can be counted. The board must meet this requirement by issuing Form 11-S to the
L230@P7: voter, according to the following schedule:
L231@P7: • Form 11-S must be issued no later than two business days after a “defective”
L232@P7: absentee ballot identification envelope is received by the board of elections
L233@P7: from the start of absentee voting (Tuesday, October 6, 2026) through the third
L234@P7: Saturday prior to the election (Saturday, October 17, 2026).
L235@P7: • Form 11-S must be issued no later than one calendar day after a “defective”
L236@P7: absentee ballot identification envelope is received by the board of elections
L237@P7: between the third Monday (Monday, October 19, 2026) and the last Friday
L238@P7: prior to the election (Friday, October 30, 2026).
L239@P7: • Form 11-S must be issued on the same day that a “defective” absentee ballot
L240@P7: identification envelope is received by the board of elections between the

L242@P8: Saturday prior to the election (Saturday, October 31, 2026) and 7:30 p.m. on

L244@P8: When a phone number or email address is on file with the board of elections, the board

L249@P8: PART THREE - OFFICIAL CANVASS
L250@P8: I. SCHEDULE FOR OFFICIAL CANVASS10
L251@P8: A board must begin the Official Canvass no earlier than the fifth day after the election
L252@P8: (Sunday, November 8, 2026) nor later than the fifteenth day after the election
L253@P8: (Wednesday, November 18, 2026). Each board must complete the Official Canvass and
L254@P8: certify no later than the twenty-first day after the election (Tuesday, November 24,
L255@P8: 2026).
L256@P8: II. PREPARING FOR OFFICIAL CANVASS
L257@P8: Boards of elections may start processing cured absentee ballots that were originally
L258@P8: received by the close of polls on Election Day and UOCAVA absentee ballots that arrive
L259@P8: after Election Day before the board starts the Official Canvass, but boards must not
L260@P8: count such ballots until the Official Canvas begins.11 Board members and employees are
L261@P8: prohibited from disclosing partial or final results of any contest in the election between
L262@P8: the completion of the Unofficial Canvass and the certification of official results.
L263@P8: III. INSTRUCTIONS FOR OFFICIAL CANVASS
L264@P8: Each board of elections must follow the instructions for pre-canvass activity outlined in
L265@P8: Chapter 10, Section 10.04 of the Election Official Manual. Boards must also follow the
L266@P8: rules and procedures for conducting the Official Canvass outlined in Chapter 10, Section
L267@P8: 10.05 of the Election Official Manual. Prior to the tenth day after Election Day, each
L268@P8: board must reconcile results with records from the pollbooks and voter registration
L269@P8: system to ensure that only one ballot per voter is counted.12 This includes ensuring that
L270@P8-9: 9 R.C. 3509.06(D)(3)(b). 10 R.C. 3505.32(A). 11 See R.C. 3509.06(F); R.C. 3513.22(A). 12 R.C. 3505.32(D).Office of the Ohio Secretary of State 10 | page
L271@P9: all returned absentee ballots are entered in the voter registration system and reconciling
L272@P9: the list of voters whose ballots were returned with the number of physical ballots
L273@P9: returned.
L274@P9: IV. FORMS FOR OFFICIAL CERTIFICATION
L275@P9: After the Unofficial Canvass, the Secretary of State’s office will provide the forms for
L276@P9: reporting official results. All certifications and reports must be signed by the appropriate
L277@P9: board personnel before the board submits them to the Secretary of State’s office,
L278@P9: another board of elections, or another public entity.
L279@P9: Each board of elections must submit the signature form to certify the official election
L280@P9: results, including the absentee and provisional ballot reports, to the Secretary of State’s
L281@P9: office.
L282@P9: A. Certification and Reporting of Official Results13
L283@P9: Each board of elections must complete and provide all the following the same day it
L284@P9: completes its official certification but no later than Tuesday, November 24, 2026:
L285@P9: • Official Vote Total Summary Report
L286@P9: • Group Detail Report (if not included with Summary Report)
L287@P9: • Signature form
L288@P9: • Report forms
L289@P9: • Electronic turnout detail by precinct
L290@P9: • Statement of Votes Cast (SOVC) report
L291@P9: • Absentee and provisional ballot report
L292@P9: Each board of elections must submit these reports to Results@OhioSoS.gov as soon as
L293@P9: the board completes its official certification. The Official Vote Total Summary Report
L294@P9: must be clearly labeled “[County]’s Official Canvass,” and it must contain only vote totals
L295@P9: for that county. Boards must not delay submitting the official certification forms because
L296@P9: of a potential recount. Every board must maintain a copy of each of its completed
L297@P9: certification and report forms.
L298@P9: The board of elections for the most populous county in any multicounty jurisdiction or
L299@P9: district must generate a separate report from its voting system, create a report outside
L300@P9: its voting system, or use a reporting form that will be provided after the Unofficial
L301@P9: Canvass. This report must be clearly labeled “[County’s] Official Canvass – Most

L303@P10: Populous County.” The report must include the total number of votes recorded for the
